title: Kotl Architecture
intro: Teal is Kotl, our product. Purple is Slurm. Gray is everything else off the shelf, plus the hardware. The dot on each box is its build status; click a box for exactly what's happening.
latest: Latest: M1 scripts are written (deploy/). They're waiting for the admin to run them; then verify-m1.sh turns the M1 parts green.

zones.label: SLURM · off-the-shelf scheduler
zones.sub: not part of Kotl · runs on the workstation · Kotl uses only its normal commands

steps.name: Submit
steps.text: Claude runs kotl firesim submit my-job/ --wait over SSH. Kotl checks the folder against the template and refuses a job that can't end on its own.

steps.name: Queue
steps.text: The CLI hands the job to Slurm with sbatch. Slurm orders it by priority and estimates its start from the ETAs ahead of it.

steps.name: Start
steps.text: A board license frees up. Slurm's job starter runs job.sh, which hands over to Kotl's launcher.

steps.name: Claim board
steps.text: The launcher claims an idle, healthy board in the registry, marks it busy, and adds this job's key to the board's PC.

steps.name: Run
steps.text: The FireSim adapter runs your own FireSim, from your Chipyard, as you. It reflashes the board and boots Linux using the job key.

steps.name: Over ETA
steps.text: Still running past its ETA? Nothing is killed. The notifier (started every minute by a systemd timer) asks Slurm, then tells the owner and their Claude.

steps.name: Hang
steps.text: A guard trips: idle, the expect timeout, or the owner's --max. The end step kills the simulation, removes the job key, marks the job hung or over max, and tells the owner.

steps.name: Power off
steps.text: Normal end: run.sh prints its KOTL RESULT line and the system powers off. FireSim returns, the launcher removes the job key, frees the board and exits. Slurm records succeeded or failed, then its epilog repeats the end step as a backup.

steps.name: Results
steps.text: The collect step fills the job folder. Claude runs kotl fetch to pull it to the user's PC.

steps.name: Meanwhile
steps.text: Every 5 minutes Slurm runs Kotl's health check, which probes the board over the SSH path and marks a bad one down.

steps.name: Request
steps.text: From your own Chipyard you type firesim infrasetup, as always. Kotl's wrapper sees you hold no board and queues a job, the same queue as batch jobs.

steps.name: Start
steps.text: Your turn: Slurm starts the job. The launcher claims the board and adds this job's key to its PC.

steps.name: Boot
steps.text: The wrapper now runs your real firesim infrasetup, then runworkload, inside the job and as you. Your FireSim reaches the PC with the job key.

steps.name: Attach
steps.text: kotl firesim attach <job> checks you own it and opens the console on PC 1. Run your application.

steps.name: Over ETA
steps.text: Still working past your ETA? You get a notice, and the queue gets new estimates. Nothing is killed.

steps.name: End
steps.text: Type poweroff in the sim, or run firesim kill. runworkload returns and the job ends: Kotl removes the job key, closes leftover sessions and frees the board. Slurm's epilog repeats this as a backup.

steps.name: Forgot
steps.text: Walked away? After the idle time with no console activity, the launcher runs the end step, frees the board and tells you.

steps.name: Request
steps.text: You run kotl board program vcu118-pc1 --bitstream new.bit. It becomes a Slurm job at the admin-only maintenance level.

steps.name: Drain
steps.text: Slurm starts it when it's first in line; the launcher marks PC 1 draining in the registry. A running job there finishes normally, or you cancel it.

steps.name: Program
steps.text: The launcher runs the Program / reset adapter, which loads the bitstream over the kotl SSH path.

steps.name: Verify
steps.text: The board-test adapter checks XDMA with a quick DMA read/write, and the health check confirms the board.

steps.name: Return
steps.text: The registry records the new bitstream and marks PC 1 idle. Users' jobs flow back in, and you get a done notice.

steps.name: Summary
steps.text: What Kotl installs or edits on each machine. Every change is made by a deploy/ script that the admin runs, and each script can undo its own changes.

steps.name: Workstation
steps.text: The workstation carries almost everything: Slurm, MariaDB, the kotl account, Kotl's programs and a few small config snippets.

steps.name: FPGA PC
steps.text: On the PC: a kotl account, one helper script and one sudoers line. sshd stays as it is until full lockdown.

steps.name: Users
steps.text: Nothing system-wide for users; their Chipyard is only read.

overview.title: Whole picture
bullets: Teal is Kotl, our product: the code we write and maintain, plus a plugin in each user's Claude.
Purple is Slurm, off the shelf. Kotl talks to it in exactly four places, through its normal commands.
Gray is everything else off the shelf (FireSim, the workstation's OS) and the hardware.
Everything reaching the FPGA PCs goes through the kotl key or a job key that works only while that job runs.
Users keep their own Chipyard and FireSim. Plain firesim commands go through Kotl's wrapper, which queues them; a job ends when the simulated Linux powers off.
The core is a generic board lease (queue, claim, SSH access, end step). Adapters add task knowledge: FireSim now; program/reset and board tests later.
overview.hint: Click any box for its commands and files. The tabs show what Kotl is, where it meets Slurm, and three flows step by step.

kotllens.title: What's Kotl
kotllens.what: Everything highlighted in teal: the code we write, install and maintain.
bullets: Entry: the kotl CLI with its firesim wrapper, console attach, the job template, and the Kotl plugin for Claude Code.
Core: the board lease (launcher + PC access), board registry, health check, ETA notifier, job results, the kotl SSH key. Later: power monitor, usage dashboard. Parked: same-design pick.
Adapters (task-specific, on the lease): FireSim now. Later: program/reset, board tests. Anything else can use kotl lease or kotl run directly.
kotllens.note: Not Kotl: Slurm (scheduling), each user's FireSim (simulation), the workstation OS (sudo, systemd timers, OpenSSH) and the FPGA PCs. Kotl only uses their normal commands and config files.

slurmlens.title: Where Kotl meets Slurm
slurmlens.what: Four places, numbered like the purple badges. Everything else in Kotl never talks to Slurm.
ordered: Queue ↔ kotl CLI. The CLI submits (sbatch), cancels (scancel) and lists (squeue). Slurm orders the queue by priority and counts boards as licenses.

Job starter → launcher. When a board is free, Slurm runs job.sh, which asks Kotl's launcher to claim it. A cancel arrives as a signal. After the job, Slurm's epilog runs Kotl's end step again as a backup.
Health runner → health check. Slurm runs Kotl's health.sh every 5 minutes.
Accounting → notifier and dashboard. The notifier asks who is running and when queued jobs will start; the dashboard (later) reads history with sacct.
slurmlens.note: Kotl never changes Slurm's code. It only uses Slurm's commands and a few lines of slurm.conf.

remote.title: Remote user PC
remote.what: A user's own machine. Builds happen here; runs happen through the workstation.
bullets: Builds the design with their own Chipyard and FireSim (bitstream + driver).
Has a normal Linux account on the workstation, reached over SSH.
Never holds a lasting key to the FPGA PCs; a job key works only during their job.
What they get: plain firesim keeps working, kotl new gives the template, and Claude knows the rest.

local.title: Local user
local.what: Same flow, but the user is already logged into the workstation.
bullets: Builds with their own Chipyard on the workstation.
Types plain firesim commands as before; the wrapper queues them. Or uses kotl directly.
Gets no more FPGA access than a remote user.

admin.title: Admin (you)
admin.what: Root on the workstation. Runs maintenance and hears about stuck jobs and sick boards.
bullets: Can cancel any job.
Gets the 2× ETA alerts and board-down alerts.
Runs maintenance through Kotl, so it never collides with a user's job.
Grants the "urgent" priority level.

lines.c: kotl cancel 1234            # root can cancel any job

plugin.title: Kotl plugin for Claude Code
plugin.what: Part of Kotl, installed in every user's Claude Code. It makes the right path the easy one.
bullets: Skill: teaches Claude the job template (kotl new), the kotl commands, and to write expect scripts that always have a timeout.
Hook before a tool runs: checks that firesim resolves to Kotl's wrapper, and warns if a job folder doesn't follow the template.
Hook at session start: shows the queue, your jobs and their start estimates.
Shows over-ETA and start-time notices; fetches results when a job ends.
plugin.note: Convenience only. The SSH lockdown and the end step are the real enforcement.

cli.title: kotl CLI
cli.what: The one command for everything. It also puts a thin firesim wrapper first on everyone's PATH, so plain FireSim commands from your own Chipyard go through the queue.
bullets: Generic: kotl lease / kotl release hold a board for any tool; kotl run -- <cmd> holds it while one command runs.
firesim wrapper: firesim infrasetup with no board held queues a job and waits; once the board is yours, it runs your real FireSim inside the job. runworkload returning or firesim kill ends the job.
Your FireSim's own deploy/ stays where it is: FireSim's setup adds it to the end of PATH, so the wrapper is found first and calls it.
kotl new my-job copies the job template (marshal.json, run.sh, kotl.json).
Refuses a batch job that can't end on its own (no run script, no --expect), and says how to fix it.
Cancel works only for the job's owner or root.
ETA is required: --eta, "eta" in kotl.json, or KOTL_ETA for plain firesim. Without one, Kotl refuses and says how to give it.

lines.k: # plain FireSim: the wrapper queues for you

lines.o: kotl: waiting for a VCU118 (1 ahead, ~40 min)… got vcu118-pc1 (job 1240)
kotl: type poweroff in the sim or run firesim kill to free the board
kotl: job 1240 done · VCU118 freed · results in /srv/kotl/out/you/1240/

lines.k: # or the job template, one command

lines.c: kotl lease --eta 1h  |  kotl release  |  kotl run --eta 30m -- <cmd>
kotl status | history | cancel <job> | logs <job> -f | fetch <job>
kotl board list | drain | program | reset <board>

lines.k: # --time is the ETA (kotl.json, or the default). --max and --idle are enforced by the launcher.

attach.title: Console attach
attach.what: How a user reaches the simulated system's console without getting a shell on the FPGA PC.
bullets: Runs as kotl through the sudo rule and checks you own the job.
Opens only FireSim's console session on the job's board.
While your job runs you can also use your job key directly; it stops working when the job ends.
Console activity is what the idle guard watches. Detach and reattach any time.

lines.o: attached to job 1235 on vcu118-pc1 · detach: Ctrl-a d

launcher.title: Launcher · board lease
launcher.what: The core of Kotl: a generic board lease. It knows nothing about FireSim. Slurm starts it for every job; it claims a board, gives the owner SSH access for the job's lifetime, and always cleans up.
bullets: Confirms the Slurm job is real and belongs to the caller.
Start: claims an idle, healthy board in the registry, then adds this job's key to the board's PC.
During: the owner (and any tool they run: FireSim, Vivado, scripts) reaches the PC with the job key. An adapter can add start/end triggers and checks.
The lease ends when the work ends: the adapter's end trigger (e.g. FireSim's runworkload returns), kotl release, the command of kotl run exits, or cancel. No timer closes it.
Guards: idle (no job-key SSH session and no processes on the PC for N minutes) and the owner's --max (default 2× ETA).

End step, every time, same for every adapter: the adapter's polite stop if it has one (e.g. firesim kill), then remove the job key, end this job's sessions and processes (in full lockdown: every process of the PC account), record why, free the board. Slurm's epilog repeats it as a backup.
Records setup time on every job, for the parked same-design idea.

lines.o: lease 1250 on vcu118-pc1 · ssh vcu118-pc1 works until you release

lines.k: # or tie it to one command: the lease ends when the command exits

registry.title: Board registry
registry.what: One record per board: its state, what's loaded on it, its health and power.
bullets: States: down → idle → setting up → busy → draining → maintenance → idle.
The launcher claims a board here in one step, so two jobs never share a board.
The health check and power monitor write to it; kotl board list reads it.
A single SQLite file. No service to keep running.

health.title: Health check
health.what: A Kotl script that Slurm runs every 5 minutes. It checks each board over the kotl SSH path.
bullets: Ping, SSH as kotl, lspci shows the Xilinx card, XDMA driver loaded.
Flags leftover work on a board the registry says is idle.
Lockdown mode (lockdown in /etc/kotl/kotl.conf): in soft, work on a board with no lease (e.g. a password login) only warns the admin; in full, it marks the board for checking.
On failure: tries reloading the driver once. Still failing: marks the board down, holds back its Slurm slot, alerts the admin.
Puts the board back on its own when checks pass again.

notifier.title: ETA notifier
notifier.what: A short Kotl program that a systemd timer starts every minute. It asks Slurm who is running and for how long, then sends notices. It never kills anything.
bullets: Job passes its ETA: tells the owner through their Claude plugin and kotl status.
Job passes 2× its ETA: also tells the admin, the same way.
Queued jobs whose start estimate slipped: tells those users.
Board down or back: tells the admin.
Channel: the Claude plugin only for now (no email or chat). Notices wait in a per-user inbox that the plugin and kotl status read.

term.host: under the hood · each pass, as kotl

lines.k: # job id, user, time used, ETA (time limit), start estimate

results.title: Job results
results.what: One folder per job, filled by the end step and the adapter's collect step.
bullets: Local users read it through ~/kotl-results. Remote users run kotl fetch; the Claude plugin does it for them.
kotl writes, the owner reads. Other users can't see it.
Deleted automatically after 30 days.

lines.c: ssh ws kotl logs 1235 -f     # follow a running job's console

power.title: Power monitor
power.what: Reads each board's power on a timer. Never queued, never blocks a job.
bullets: A systemd timer starts it every minute; it reads over the kotl SSH path. No agent on the PCs.
Source to decide later: the board's on-board power sensors, or a smart PDU per PC.
Stores readings in the registry. Alerts if a board draws power while idle, or goes over a limit.

dashboard.title: Usage dashboard
dashboard.what: A small web page on the workstation. Build it once the queue is running.
bullets: Board-hours per user per week, from Slurm's history.
Queue wait times, and how often jobs overrun their ETA.
Board state history and power per board, from the registry.

affinity.title: Same-design pick
affinity.what: On hold: prefer a board that already has the job's bitstream loaded, to save setup time.
bullets: FireSim says to re-run setup before every simulation, so setup can't simply be skipped.
The registry already knows what's loaded, so this would only be a board-pick rule.
Revisit once recorded setup times show it's worth it. No priority boost either way.

fsmod.title: FireSim adapter
fsmod.what: A thin layer on the lease that teaches Kotl FireSim's lifecycle. It has no FireSim of its own: it calls your FireSim, from your Chipyard, as you, inside your job. All FireSim knowledge lives here; the core has none.
bullets: Path: you → wrapper (this adapter) → your FireSim → job key → the board's PC. The adapter never talks to the board itself.
Start trigger: firesim infrasetup (through the wrapper) with no lease held starts one and waits for the board.
End trigger: firesim runworkload returning, or firesim kill, ends the lease.
Prepare: copies your config_runtime.yaml into the job folder with the run farm pointed at the claimed board and PC account.
Check (batch): the job follows the template: a FireMarshal run/command (powers off when done) or --expect. Interactive jobs are allowed, with the idle guard.
Polite stop: firesim kill before the core's end step. Collect: copies results, reads the KOTL RESULT line from uartlog.
What users get: plain firesim keeps working, kotl new (the template), a one-page guide, the Claude skill, and refusals that say exactly what to fix.
Board smoke test (M3): FireSim's stock linux-poweroff on xilinx_vcu118_firesim_rocket_singlecore_4GB_no_nic.

term.host: under the hood · as you, inside job 1240

lines.k: # on kill, cancel or a tripped guard

program.title: Program / reset
program.what: Admin adapter on the lease: load a bitstream or reset a board outside FireSim.
bullets: Takes a lease at the admin-only maintenance level, after the board is drained, so it never interrupts a user.
Programs or resets over the job key, then records the new bitstream in the registry.
The lease's end step cleans up the same way as for any job.

drvtest.title: Board tests
drvtest.what: Deep check of an FPGA PC and its board, as an adapter on the lease, before the board goes back in the pool.
bullets: Loads the XDMA driver, runs a quick DMA read/write test, records the driver version.
Runs after maintenance, a PC reboot or a failed health check, and optionally on a schedule.
The 5-minute health check stays a quick core probe; this is the thorough one, holding a lease so it never meets a user's job.

lines.o: xdma loaded · DMA read/write ok · driver 2024.1

key.title: kotl SSH key · job keys
key.what: The only paths from the workstation to the FPGA PCs: Kotl's own key, and short-lived job keys that Kotl adds and removes.
bullets: The kotl private key lives in /home/kotl/.ssh, readable only by the kotl account. Kotl uses it to grant and remove job keys, for health checks and for cleanup.
A job key lets the job's owner and their FireSim into the PC's FireSim account, only while the job runs (see PC access).
FPGA PCs: in full lockdown only kotl, virtex-host (job keys) and the admin, keys only. In soft lockdown (now) virtex-host's password and existing keys still work.
A new PC joins by adding the kotl key, the key helper and a registry entry.

lines.c: ssh vcu118-pc1 hostname        # as a normal user, no job running

queue.title: Queue + priority
queue.what: Slurm's queue holds waiting jobs and orders them. Kotl's CLI uses it through normal Slurm commands.
bullets: Each board type is a license, counted per board (vcu118:1 today, one board). A job needs one to start.

Priority (rough sketch, tune later): fair-share + waiting time + an "urgent" level only the admin grants. Maintenance has its own admin-only level. Fair-share uses Slurm accounting (slurmdbd + MariaDB on the workstation).
The ETA is required and becomes the job's time limit; Slurm uses it to estimate start times.
Never kills a job for passing its ETA. Only the owner or root can cancel.

starter.title: Job starter
starter.what: The part of Slurm that runs each job and signals it. Here it runs only on the workstation.
bullets: When a board license is free, runs job.sh as the user; it asks Kotl's launcher (as kotl) to claim the board and grant access.
On cancel: sends a stop signal, waits up to 2 minutes (KillWait), then force-stops.
After every job, runs Kotl's epilog: the end step again, as a backup.
Records the job as succeeded or failed from the exit code.

runner.title: Health runner
runner.what: Slurm runs Kotl's health check every 5 minutes. Two lines of slurm.conf.

acct.title: Accounting
acct.what: Slurm's accounting database. Answers who is running, for how long and when queued jobs start, and keeps the history.

os.title: Workstation OS
os.what: The workstation's own Linux pieces that Kotl relies on.
bullets: sudo: one rule lets users run exactly two Kotl programs as kotl.
systemd timers: start the notifier (and later the power monitor) every minute.
OpenSSH: carries the kotl key to the FPGA PCs.
Accounts: users in kotl-users; the kotl service account.
Full list of what Kotl changes here: the System files tab.

firesim.title: FireSim
firesim.what: Each user's own FireSim, in their own Chipyard. Kotl doesn't install or change it; it runs it inside the user's job.
bullets: Users keep building bitstreams and drivers in their own Chipyard. The driver is built from the user's tree, so custom target configs just work.
Runs as the user, inside their Slurm job. It reaches the board's PC with the job key, which works only while the job runs.
Keeps each simulation's console in a screen session on the PC, and notices when it disappears.
Workloads come from FireMarshal: the run script does the work, then the system powers off.

pc1.title: VCU118 PC 1
pc1.what: Hosts the lab's VCU118, at 192.168.1.2 (vcu118-pc1 in kotl's SSH config). Reachable only from the workstation.
bullets: Runs sshd, the XDMA driver, FireSim's helper scripts and a small key helper. No other Kotl code.
Accounts: kotl, virtex-host (FireSim; gets job keys) and the admin.

Soft lockdown for now: password logins to virtex-host still work for people who know it. Take a lease (kotl lease) before touching the FPGA, or you may break a running job. Later: full lockdown with a separate admin account.
Reboots are harmless: the health check sees it come back.

pc2.title: VCU118 PC 2
pc2.what: Later: a second VCU118 PC. Same as PC 1 when it arrives; then the license goes to vcu118:2.

tooling.title: Repo tooling
tooling.what: What keeps this view honest: the status file, test tags and a commit check. Not drawn on the diagram.
bullets: status.json next to this page holds every part's build status.
Every test is tagged with the part it covers; tools/status.py turns test results into tested or failing.
A pre-commit check refuses a commit that changes a part's code without updating its status.

more.title: More boards
bullets: Add a PC: sshd + driver, the kotl key, a registry entry, and one more Slurm license.
Different board types get their own license name (for example u250:2).
Servers without FPGAs can join for health and power monitoring only.

access.title: PC access (job keys)
access.what: Lets a job's owner, and their own FireSim, reach the board's PC for exactly as long as the job runs. No timers: access follows the job.
bullets: Job start: the launcher makes a key for this job and adds it to the PC's FireSim account (virtex-host), using the kotl key.

Job end (adapter end trigger, kotl release, cancel or a tripped guard): removes the key, closes this job's SSH sessions and stops its simulations, then the board is freed. In full lockdown it kills every process of the PC account.
Backup: Slurm's epilog runs the same end step after every job, even if the launcher crashed. It is safe to run twice.
Only the board this job claimed gets the key. Outside a job, users can't reach any PC.

Lockdown mode (lockdown in /etc/kotl/kotl.conf): soft (now): password logins to virtex-host still work and other keys stay; the end step kills only this job's sessions and simulations. full (later): separate admin account, virtex-host key-only, end step kills every virtex-host process.

lines.c: ssh vcu118-pc1 kotl-keys add 1240 'restrict,pty ssh-ed25519 AAAA… kotl-job-1240'
ssh vcu118-pc1 kotl-keys remove 1240   # removes the key, ends its sessions

access.note: The PC-side helper is a small script installed by the admin in M1. No other Kotl code runs on the PCs.

sys-summary.title: What Kotl changes, per machine
sys-summary.what: Every system file, account and package that Kotl adds or edits, grouped by machine. Step through the tabs above. All of it is installed by scripts under deploy/ that the admin runs, never by Kotl itself.
bullets: Workstation (comparch): Slurm + MariaDB + munge, the kotl account and group, /opt/kotl, /etc/kotl, /srv/kotl, /var/lib/kotl, a sudoers rule, PATH and SSH client snippets, and a systemd timer.
VCU118 PC 1: in soft lockdown (now) only a kotl account, one helper script and one sudoers line. sshd and virtex-host's password are untouched. Full lockdown adds one sshd file.
Users: nothing system-wide on their PCs, and nothing written into their Chipyard or home folder.
Each script has an --undo that removes exactly what it added.
sys-summary.note: Click a step to see that machine's list; open a file card for its contents. Paths marked (sketch) are tested in M1 before use.

sudo deploy/<script> --undo      # each script removes what it added

sys-ws.title: Workstation (comparch)
sys-ws.what: Everything Kotl adds on the workstation. Nothing outside these paths changes.
bullets: Packages: slurm-wlm, slurmdbd, munge, mariadb-server, expect (new · M1)
Accounts: system user kotl, group kotl-users (all regular users), Slurm's own slurm user (new · M1, deploy/accounts.sh)
/etc/slurm/slurm.conf: the single-node Slurm config: license, priority, ETA, KillWait, health check, Epilog (new · M1)
/etc/slurm/slurmdbd.conf: accounting daemon, using the MariaDB database slurm_acct_db (new · M1)
/etc/slurm/cgroup.conf: lets Slurm track every process of a job (new · M1)
/etc/munge/munge.key: Slurm's local auth key (owner munge, 0400) (new · M1)
/etc/sudoers.d/kotl: users may run exactly two Kotl programs as kotl (new · M1)
/etc/profile.d/kotl.sh: puts the firesim wrapper first on PATH (new · M3)
/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/kotl.conf: ssh vcu118-pc1 uses your job key during a lease (new · M3)
/etc/kotl/kotl.conf: Kotl settings: lockdown mode, admin, PC account, idle time (new · M1)
/etc/systemd/system/kotl-notifier.{service,timer}: runs the notifier every minute (new · M4)
/opt/kotl/: Kotl's programs. M1 puts in epilog.sh and health.sh as no-op placeholders (Slurm needs them to exist); launch, attach, bin/firesim and adapters/ follow in M2–M3 (new · M1–M3)
/var/lib/kotl/: board registry kotl.db (owner kotl; folder M1, database M2) (new · M1)
/srv/kotl/: jobs/ and out/<user>/<job>/, owner-only, deleted after 30 days (folders M1) (new · M1)
/run/kotl/keys/: job keys while a lease is held (tmpfs, gone on reboot) (new · M3)
/home/kotl/.ssh/: the kotl key and its host alias (new · M1)
Services enabled: munge, mariadb, slurmdbd, slurmctld, slurmd (M1)

sys-pc.title: VCU118 PC 1 (192.168.1.2)
sys-pc.what: Kotl's footprint on the FPGA PC is deliberately tiny. In soft lockdown (now), sshd, passwords and existing keys are untouched.
bullets: Accounts: user kotl (key login only, password locked) (new · M1, deploy/pc/setup.sh, run on the PC)
/home/kotl/.ssh/authorized_keys: the kotl public key (new · M1)
/usr/local/bin/kotl-keys: adds and removes job keys; the only Kotl code on the PC (new · M3)
/etc/sudoers.d/kotl: kotl may run only kotl-keys, as virtex-host (new · M3)
/home/virtex-host/.ssh/authorized_keys: Kotl adds and removes only its own kotl-job-* lines; your lines stay (edited at run time · M3)
Full lockdown only (later): /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/kotl.conf (keys only, AllowUsers) and the separate admin account. Not installed now.
Not touched: FireSim's files, the XDMA driver, virtex-host's password, the sims folder.

sys-users.title: Users' PCs and folders
sys-users.what: Kotl changes nothing system-wide for users, and writes nothing into their Chipyard.
bullets: Their Chipyard and FireSim: read only. Kotl copies config_runtime.yaml into /srv/kotl/jobs/<job>/ and changes the copy.
Their home folder: nothing, unless they run kotl new my-job (creates that folder) or kotl fetch (downloads results).
Their own PC: only the Claude Code plugin, if they install it (M5).

slurmconf.name: slurm.conf
slurmconf.desc: Rendered by deploy/slurm/install.sh from deploy/slurm/slurm.conf.in (host and CPUs filled in)
slurmconf.body:
# managed by kotl (deploy/slurm/install.sh). Edit deploy/slurm/slurm.conf.in in the repo, then re-run.
# Single node: the workstation runs the controller, the job runner and accounting.
ClusterName=kotl
SlurmctldHost=@HOST@
SlurmUser=slurm
AuthType=auth/munge
StateSaveLocation=/var/spool/slurmctld
SlurmdSpoolDir=/var/spool/slurmd
SlurmctldPidFile=/run/slurmctld.pid
SlurmdPidFile=/run/slurmd.pid
SlurmctldLogFile=/var/log/slurm/slurmctld.log
SlurmdLogFile=/var/log/slurm/slurmd.log
ProctrackType=proctrack/cgroup
TaskPlugin=task/none
ReturnToService=2
SchedulerType=sched/backfill
SelectType=select/cons_tres
SelectTypeParameters=CR_Core

NodeName=@HOST@ CPUs=@CPUS@ State=UNKNOWN
PartitionName=fpga Nodes=@HOST@ Default=YES MaxTime=UNLIMITED State=UP

# Boards are counted as licenses, one per board
Licenses=vcu118:1

# Priority (rough sketch, tune later)
PriorityType=priority/multifactor
PriorityWeightFairshare=10000
PriorityWeightAge=1000
PriorityWeightQOS=100000
PriorityDecayHalfLife=7-0

# The ETA is the job's time limit; never kill for passing it; give clean stops time
OverTimeLimit=UNLIMITED
KillWait=120

# Kotl's end step after every job (backup); a no-op until M2
Epilog=/opt/kotl/epilog.sh

# Kotl's health check; a no-op until M4
HealthCheckProgram=/opt/kotl/health.sh
HealthCheckInterval=300

# History and fair-share, through slurmdbd + MariaDB
AccountingStorageType=accounting_storage/slurmdbd
AccountingStorageHost=localhost
AccountingStorageEnforce=associations,limits,qos
JobAcctGatherType=jobacct_gather/linux

healthconf.name: slurm.conf (excerpt)
healthconf.desc: The two lines that make Slurm run Kotl's health check

jobsh.name: job.sh
jobsh.desc: What Slurm runs for every Kotl job
jobsh.body:
#!/bin/sh
# Slurm runs this as the submitting user, inside their job.
# 1) Kotl (as kotl) claims a board and adds this job's key to its PC
sudo -u kotl /opt/kotl/launch start "$SLURM_JOB_ID" "$1" || exit 1
# 2) the adapter's hooks, or your kotl run command; runs as you
/opt/kotl/run-adapter "$SLURM_JOB_ID" "$1"; rc=$?
# 3) end step: stop leftovers, remove the key, free the board
sudo -u kotl /opt/kotl/launch end "$SLURM_JOB_ID"
exit $rc

sudoers.name: kotl
sudoers.desc: The only things users may run as kotl
sudoers.body:
# Users in kotl-users may run exactly two programs as kotl
%kotl-users ALL=(kotl) NOPASSWD: /opt/kotl/launch, /opt/kotl/attach

modules.name: adapters/firesim/
modules.desc: An adapter = a few optional hooks on the lease. The core's end step always runs after them.
modules.body:
/opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/
  triggers  # infrasetup starts a lease · runworkload returns / firesim kill ends it
  check     # batch: does the job follow the template? (run script, --expect, or interactive)
  prepare   # copy config_runtime.yaml for the claimed board and PC account
  stop      # polite stop: firesim kill (the core then kills everything anyway)
  collect   # copy results, read the KOTL RESULT line

# no adapter at all: kotl lease / kotl run -- <cmd>

registry.name: kotl.db
registry.desc: Board registry: one SQLite file, one row per board
registry.body:
CREATE TABLE boards (
  name           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- vcu118-pc1
  host           TEXT NOT NULL,     -- SSH host name
  type           TEXT NOT NULL,     -- vcu118 (matches the Slurm license)
  state          TEXT NOT NULL,     -- down | idle | setting_up | busy | draining | maintenance
  job_id         INTEGER,           -- Slurm job holding it
  bitstream      TEXT,              -- design currently loaded
  driver_version TEXT,
  last_healthy   TEXT,              -- time of last good check
  power_watts    REAL               -- later
);

healthsh.name: health.sh
healthsh.desc: Kotl's health check; Slurm runs it every 5 minutes (sketch)
healthsh.body:
#!/bin/sh
# Runs as root under Slurm. Checks each board over the kotl SSH path.
for board in $(kotl-registry boards); do
  host=$(kotl-registry host "$board")
  if sudo -u kotl ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 "$host" 'lspci -d 10ee: | grep -q . && lsmod | grep -q xdma'; then
    kotl-registry mark "$board" healthy
  else
    kotl-registry mark "$board" down   # also holds back its Slurm slot and alerts the admin
  fi
done

skill.name: SKILL.md
skill.desc: Teaches Claude how to use Kotl
skill.body:
---
name: kotl
description: Run FireSim jobs on the lab's FPGAs through Kotl: submit, check, cancel, fetch results.
---
# Kotl
- Never run firesim directly. Use kotl.
- Submit in the background; you'll be told when it ends:
  ssh ws kotl firesim submit --hwdb <hw> --workload <wl> --eta <est> --max <limit> --wait
- The workload must power off by itself, or pass --expect <script>.
- Expect scripts always set a timeout and exit 2 on timeout.
- When a job ends: ssh ws kotl fetch <job>, then read status.json first.

kotljson.name: kotl.json
kotljson.desc: Template · Kotl settings for this job. The wrapper also reads it from your FireSim deploy folder.
kotljson.body:
{
  "mode": "batch",          // or "interactive" (idle guard always on)
  "eta": "1h",              // required; queue estimate, never kills the job
  "max": "2h",              // optional hang guard (default 2x eta)
  "idle": "30m",            // free the board after this long with no console activity
  "hwdb": "xilinx_vcu118_firesim_rocket_singlecore_4GB_no_nic"
}

kotlkeys.name: kotl-keys
kotlkeys.desc: The only Kotl code on a PC: adds and removes job keys for virtex-host (sketch)
kotlkeys.body:
#!/bin/sh
# kotl-keys add <job> '<key line>' | remove <job>     runs as virtex-host (see sudoers)
AK=/home/virtex-host/.ssh/authorized_keys
case "$1" in
  add)    printf '%s\n' "$3" >> "$AK" ;;            # line ends with kotl-job-<job>
  remove) sed -i "/ kotl-job-$2\$/d" "$AK"         # only Kotl's own lines
          # end this job's sessions and its FireSim screens
          # (full lockdown: pkill -u virtex-host)
          ;;
esac

pcsudoers.desc: Lets the kotl account run only kotl-keys as virtex-host

# managed by kotl (deploy/slurm/install.sh)
# Slurm tracks each job's processes in a cgroup so cancel and the end step catch them all.
CgroupPlugin=autodetect
ConstrainCores=no
